pages.text: On a day for spreading guest bedding, Kota dragged in a quilt and tossed it onto the floor. It bunched into a mountain.
A hippo lady entered and stopped. "Oh, this quilt is a bumpy mountain!" Kota blushed. "Spreading it is hard..."
She was so big she needed two quilts. "After a long journey, I want to lie down soon." Kota tugged the bunched quilt. It did not move.
Dad put a corner in Kota's hand. "Shall we make a cloud? Flap, Float, Smooth!" Kota tilted their head. "A cloud from a quilt?"
Together, they held its corners and lifted with a flap. It floated up, then settled softly down. "Wow, like a real cloud!"
"Any mountains of wrinkles left?" Kota smoothed with both palms. Wrinkles disappeared, leaving it flat.
The second quilt went flap, float—smooth! The hippo lay down gently and closed her eyes. "I'm lying on a cloud." Kota's tail shot up.
"These are Kota's clouds!" She patted the quilt. Kota blushed right to their ears. "I'll spread tomorrow's bedding, too!"
Now Kota held each corner and counted. "One, hold! Two, flap! Three, smooth!" A quilt cloud settled in each guest room.
At night, Kota slipped under their own quilt. Dad tucked it snugly under their chin. "Neatly spread bedding brings peaceful sleep." Kota smiled beneath it. "Tomorrow, Flap, Float, Smooth!"
